title: Rocky Jordan
paragraphs: An atmospheric crime-adventure series set in Cairo, where American café owner Rocky Jordan operates the Café Tambourine and repeatedly becomes entangled in murder, espionage, and international intrigue.
Adventure/crime series about American cafe owner Rocky Jordan.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: A Man Named Jordan precursor (January 8, 1945 to April 20, 1947) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], Rocky Jordan CBS West Coast (October 31, 1948 to September 10, 1950) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], and George Raft CBS network revival (June 27, 1951 to August 22, 1951) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Cliff Howell (director, producer, and transcriber), [[person|jack-moyles|Jack Moyles]] (performer), Richard Aurandt (composer, conductor, and music), Gomer Cool (writer, radio adaptor, and story editor), Larry Roman (writer, story editor, and radio adaptor), [[person|larry-thor|Larry Thor]] (announcer, commercial spokesman, and performer), and Jay Novello (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].
The stories often return to Cairo and Egypt, murder, Cafe Tambourine, smuggling and contraband, and espionage and agents.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes A Man Named Jordan precursor, Cairo relocation and noir-adventure identity, George Raft network revival, and Mid-1950s revival auditions.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|philip-marlowe|The Adventures of Philip Marlowe]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], and [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]].
